capability: Euler buckling load recovered from an imperfection-based nonlinear column

parameters.note: nu = 0 so the plane-strain effective modulus equals E; I = b h^3/12 with b = 1.

quantity.name: Euler critical buckling load
quantity.observable: Slope of the Southwell line: the additional lateral deflection a of a geometrically imperfect column under a dead axial load satisfies a = a0 P/(P_cr - P), so a/P plotted against a is a straight line of slope 1/P_cr. P is the measured SidesetReaction at the clamp, not the nominal applied load.
quantity.supersedes: The previous result.json reported southwell_Pcr equal to the closed-form value at every imperfection level with relative_error exactly 0.0, and moose_value was null. No MOOSE quantity entered that number. Replaced 2026-08-03 before the runs below.

cantilever_fixed_free.loading: dead axial traction on the free end

fixed_pinned.loading: dead axial traction, loaded face held at disp_y = 0 (a roller)

fixed_fixed_sliding.loading: uniform prescribed disp_x on the loaded face, which holds it plane and vertical

reference.derivation: Euler column buckling. Two effective-length factors differing by 4x in K and 16x in P_cr are run so the measurement cannot accidentally agree.
reference.confirmed_from: EI verified independently in MOOSE by a transverse tip-load test: implied EI = 666.508 against the nominal 666.667, a ratio of 0.9998.

declaration_correction.what_was_wrong: The first declaration listed only two cases and labelled the disp_y = 0 loaded face 'fixed_fixed_sliding' with K = 0.5. That is wrong: holding disp_y = 0 on a vertical face removes lateral translation but not rotation, because the section slope dv/dx is unconstrained. The input implements fixed-PINNED.
declaration_correction.how_it_was_caught: The recovered Pcr was 1.3532 against the declared 2.6319, a 48% error that did not move with imperfection amplitude or mesh. A discrepancy that is insensitive to every refinement knob is a wrong reference or a wrong model, never discretization -- and 1.3532 is 0.5% from the fixed-pinned load 1.34605.
declaration_correction.what_changed: The mislabelled case is relabelled fixed-pinned against its own exact transcendental reference, and a genuine sliding clamp was added in column_clamped.i by driving the loaded face with a uniform prescribed displacement. No tolerance was altered. The suite now covers three effective lengths spanning 16x in Pcr, which is stronger evidence than the two originally declared.

tolerance.metric: relative error of the Southwell-recovered P_cr against the closed-form Euler load, for both boundary conditions
tolerance.rationale: Carried over unchanged from the original declaration. Not widened after observing the answer.

imperfection_independence.metric: relative spread of the recovered P_cr across the three imperfection amplitudes
imperfection_independence.rationale: Southwell must not depend on the imperfection used to excite it. Declared before the runs.

mesh_independence.metric: relative spread of the recovered P_cr across nx = 40, 80, 160

southwell_linearity.metric: minimum R^2 of the Southwell straight-line fit over P/P_cr in [0.3, 0.8]
southwell_linearity.rationale: A curved Southwell plot means the response is not first-mode dominated and the slope would not mean what it claims.

fit_window.rationale: Fixed before the runs. Below 0.3 the deflection is small and the fit is noise dominated; above ~0.85 the Newton solve slows at the limit point and finite-amplitude effects bend the Southwell line.
